selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main warning is given in this passage?
questions.answer: A person should not be fooled by loving only this world and forgetting the hereafter.

questions.question: Which Qur’an idea is mentioned about the life of this world?
questions.answer: The passage says that worldly things can deceive people.

questions.question: What kind of person is being spoken to in the passage?
questions.answer: It speaks to a careless self that enjoys this life too much and neglects the next life.

questions.question: What animal is used in the comparison?
questions.answer: An ostrich.

questions.question: Why is the ostrich unable to escape the hunter in the example?
questions.answer: It cannot fly away.

questions.question: What does the ostrich do when it notices the hunter?
questions.answer: It pushes its head into the sand.

questions.question: What problem still remains even after the ostrich hides its head?
questions.answer: Its large body is still out in the open where the hunter can see it.

questions.question: What happens to the ostrich’s own sight when its head is in the sand?
questions.answer: It cannot see the hunter anymore.

questions.question: What are readers being asked to do with this comparison?
questions.answer: They are being told to think carefully about it and take a lesson from it.

questions.question: In a simple cause-and-effect way, what happens when the ostrich hides its head?
questions.answer: It loses sight of the hunter while the hunter still sees it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the attractions of this world?
questions.answer: They may seem nice, but they can trick people.

questions.question: What has the heedless self forgotten?
questions.answer: It has forgotten the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the heedless self mainly chase after?
questions.answer: It chases worldly life and its pleasures.

questions.question: What comparison is used to wake the person up?
questions.answer: The person is compared to an ostrich.

questions.question: In the example, what danger does the ostrich notice?
questions.answer: It notices a hunter.

questions.question: What wrong choice does the ostrich make instead of escaping?
questions.answer: It hides its head rather than dealing with the danger.

questions.question: Does hiding its head protect the ostrich’s whole body?
questions.answer: No. Its body remains exposed.

questions.question: Who can still clearly see the ostrich?
questions.answer: The hunter can still see it.

questions.question: What has changed for the ostrich after it hides its head?
questions.answer: It no longer sees the hunter, even though the danger is still there.

questions.question: What warning does this give to people?
questions.answer: Looking away from a serious truth does not remove the truth.

questions.question: What does the passage begin with after mentioning Allah’s name?
questions.answer: It begins with the idea that worldly gain is misleading.

questions.question: Is the passage giving comfort, a warning, or a funny story?
questions.answer: It is giving a warning lesson.

questions.question: What is wrong with the self being addressed?
questions.answer: It is careless, attached to this life, and forgetful of the next life.

questions.question: What creature is chosen for the example?
questions.answer: An ostrich.
